newsitem.title: USA: Sony exec says U.S. sales hit $9.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: Sony exec says U.S. sales hit $9.5 billion.

text.p: Sony Electronics Inc President and Chief Operating Officer Carl Yankowski said the consumer electronics company expects its U.S. sales to hit $9.5 billion in the fiscal year ending March 31.

Yankowski said at the Upside Technology Summit here that the company continues to increase revenues at a double-digit rate of 10 percent or more and that businesses that are less than one year old accounted for more than half the company's sales growth in the first half of the fiscal year.
Sony Electronics Inc is a U.S. unit of Sony Corp.

Yankowski told Reuters after appearing in a panel discussion here that the company expects to continue to grow revenues at double-digit rates, helped by new businesses surrounding the convergence of multi-media technologies.
The convergence trend also creates opportunities for entirely new categories products, said Yankowski.
"It's Walkman revisited and brought up to date to the 1990s," he said in a brief interview, referring to Sony's runaway success with the introduction of the Sony Walkman portable stereo products.
Yankowski showed off a new digital video camera that enables consumers to download video files to their personal computer for editing, then reload them back into the camera for display.
